legend: Assume that you have k%%ZSMJ0%% one-dimensional segments s1,s2,…sk%%ZSMJ1%% (each segment is denoted by two integers — its endpoints). Then you can build the following graph on these segments. The graph consists of k%%ZSMJ2%% vertexes, and there is an edge between the i%%ZSMJ3%%-th and the j%%ZSMJ4%%-th vertexes (i≠j%%ZSMJ5%%) if and only if the segments si%%ZSMJ6%% and sj%%ZSMJ7%% intersect (there exists at least one point that belongs to both of them).
For example, if s1=[1,6],s2=[8,20],s3=[4,10],s4=[2,13],s5=[17,18]%%ZSMJ8%%, then the resulting graph is the following:
A tree of size m%%ZSMJ9%% is good if it is possible to choose m%%ZSMJ10%% one-dimensional segments so that the graph built on these segments coincides with this tree.
You are given a tree, you have to find its good subtree with maximum possible size. Recall that a subtree is a connected subgraph of a tree.
Note that you have to answer q%%ZSMJ11%% independent queries.
input: The first line contains one integer q%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤q≤15⋅104%%ZSMJ13%%) — the number of the queries.
The first line of each query contains one integer n%%ZSMJ14%% (2≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ15%%) — the number of vertices in the tree.

Each of the next n−1%%ZSMJ16%% lines contains two integers x%%ZSMJ17%% and y%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤x,y≤n%%ZSMJ19%%) denoting an edge between vertices x%%ZSMJ20%% and y%%ZSMJ21%%. It is guaranteed that the given graph is a tree.
It is guaranteed that the sum of all n%%ZSMJ22%% does not exceed 3⋅105%%ZSMJ23%%.
output: For each query print one integer — the maximum size of a good subtree of the given tree.
note: In the first query there is a good subtree of size 8%%ZSMJ24%%. The vertices belonging to this subtree are 9,4,10,2,5,1,6,3%%ZSMJ25%%.
